subject: Security exhibit redlines — staging gates, evidence cadence, and pen-test scope
messages:
From: Alex Greene <alex.greene@quellbio.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@quellbio.com>, procurement@quellbio.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit redlines — staging gates, evidence cadence,

Marcus / Laura / Neha —

Thanks for the draft security exhibit. Attached are QuellBio's redlines (v2) and a short spreadsheet that proposes a pen-test timing window and staging IP ranges. High-level items we need clarified before we can sign: 

1) Pen-test scope / staging access: we require assurance that penetration testing will be limited to a designated non-prod staging environment with ephemeral credentials, and that testing will be coordinated through a single point of contact. Can Redwood confirm gating controls and a 3rd-party pentest whitelist process?

2) Evidence cadence & retention: We typically ask for SOC 2 reports shared quarterly (or upon renewal) and operational evidence (audit logs, configuration snapshots) on a monthly cadence during active onboarding or a quarterly cadence thereafter. Please advise Redwood's standard retention for logs and whether 18 months retention is possible for our account.

3) Inspection & notice: QuellBio's legal prefers a 14-day notice for on-site or inspection-style requests; we'd like to see 2 weeks minimum in the exhibit.

Our legal and procurement teams are copied. If we can get a short written response to the three items above and a quick call this week (30 minutes) to agree the pen-test window, we'll move to sign.

Attachments: QuellBio_SecExhibit_Redlines_v2.docx (redline), pen-test-schedule-proposal.xlsx (IP ranges & windows)

Thanks,
Alex Greene
Head of Information Security
QuellBio

Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines — staging gates, evidence cadence,

Alex — thanks for the redlines and the spreadsheet. I pulled the core asks into a short action list below so we're aligned ahead of legal's review: 

- Pen-test scope: Redwood confirms pen-tests are limited to a named non-prod staging cluster when requested in the exhibit. We require an approved test plan and a signed statement of acceptable testing tools. We will provide ephemeral credentials and a single Eng contact for coordination.

- IP whitelisting: we can support static IP ranges for limited windows; the pen-test spreadsheet looks fine as a starting point. We'll ask infra to confirm the exact egress IPs for the staging pool and provide that to you by EOD Friday.

- Evidence cadence & retention: Our standard offering is SOC 2 annual reports and monthly operational evidence during onboarding; we can support quarterly evidence packages after onboarding. For log retention, our platform default is 12 months, but we can propose a customer-level retention of 18 months for accounts on an Enterprise plan (requires a short engineering-side config; will confirm feasibility).

- Notice period: 14 days notice for inspection/forensic-ish access is reasonable. We have a small ask to limit intrusive inspection to business hours for safety and to require mutually agreed sampling windows.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Laura / Jonas to review and propose precise exhibit language for pen-test and inspection (I'll leave the redline doc with legal).
2) Marcus to get infra egress IPs and confirm retention cost delta for 18 months.
3) Alex to confirm a 30-min call window tomorrow or Friday for pen-test coordination.

Can we do 10:00am PT Friday for a quick call?

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines — staging gates, evidence cadence,

Folks — quick legal take and suggested exhibit edits below. I left the redline file with inline comments; summary points here so engineering and security are clear on the ask.

On Thu, Oct 1, 2026 at 11:00 AM marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Pen-test scope: Redwood confirms pen-tests are limited to a named non-prod staging cluster when requested in the exhibit.

Proposed contract language (suggested replacement for current paragraph 3.2):

"Penetration Testing: Customer may request penetration testing limited to Redwood's designated non-production staging environment(s). Redwood will provide temporary, auditable access credentials and will require a written test plan at least fourteen (14) days prior to the test. Penetration testing will be restricted to the scope and IP ranges explicitly listed in the agreed test plan; Redwood will not be liable for Customer-agent activity outside the agreed scope. All testing shall be conducted during mutually agreed business hours unless otherwise approved in writing by Redwood."

Inspection / Audit Rights (replace paragraph 4.1):

"Inspection Rights: Customer may request access to evidence and audit artifacts in accordance with a documented cadence. For regular operational evidence requests (non-incident), Redwood will provide a monthly package during onboarding (first 90 days) and thereafter a quarterly package. On-site or forensic-style inspections require fourteen (14) days' prior written notice and must be limited to mutually agreed sampling windows; Redwood may designate a security liaison to supervise any live inspection."

Retention: Laura notes: Redwood's standard log retention is twelve (12) months. We are willing to offer an 18-month retention option for customers on Enterprise contracts for an additional fee. I'll circulate suggested pricing language to Marcus to include in the order form.

A couple of legal guardrails:
- We prefer to keep liability language tied to scope (no unlimited exposure for tests that go beyond the agreed plan).
- We should preserve the right to suspend access if a test causes live instability.

I've attached a tracked-changes Word with the exhibit paragraphs replaced and a short comment for engineering to confirm the staging IP behavior.

Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Attachment: Redwood_SecExhibit_Suggested_Language_v1.docx

From: Alex Greene <alex.greene@quellbio.com>

Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines — staging gates, evidence cadence,

Laura / Marcus — appreciate the rapid review and the suggested language. A couple of clarifications before we finalize: 

- The pen-test paragraph looks good. One ask: will Redwood commit to providing the staging IPs and a contact at least seven (7) business days prior to the test (we need time to schedule our vendor)? Marcus indicated EOD Friday for egress IPs — that will help.

- Retention: QuellBio strongly prefers 18 months of log retention, not an optional paid add-on. Our security operations needs 18 months as a baseline. Is there a technical reason Redwood cannot set 18 months as an account-level default for Enterprise customers? If it's just an operational cost issue, we can discuss in procurement but would prefer it in the exhibit.

- Evidence cadence: monthly during onboarding, quarterly thereafter is acceptable. Please confirm how evidence packages will be delivered (SFTP, secure Drive link, or an API endpoint).

If those three items are answered, we can update our redline to reflect Laura's proposed language and sign. We can take the 30-min call off-line if needed.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Greene
Head of Information Security, QuellBio
